user.title: Add Hearth Companion
user.description:
**Recommended: MQTT auto-discovery** — If both Home Assistant and Hearth are connected to the same MQTT broker, your device will be discovered automatically. You don't need to do anything here — just make sure:

1. MQTT is configured in Home Assistant
2. Hearth's companion is running and connected to the same MQTT broker
3. Wait a moment — the device will appear as a notification

If auto-discovery isn't working, you can connect manually via the **Local API** below. This requires Hearth's Local API to be enabled (Settings → Companion → Local API) and only supports notifications.

menu_options.local_api: Connect via Local API (manual, notifications only)

mqtt_help.title: MQTT Auto-Discovery Troubleshooting
mqtt_help.description:
For MQTT auto-discovery to work:

1. **Home Assistant** must have MQTT configured and connected to a broker (e.g. Mosquitto)
2. **Hearth** must be connected to the **same** MQTT broker — check Settings → Companion → MQTT
3. The Hearth **companion sidecar** must be running — check the status pill on Hearth's dashboard (should say 'Running')
4. Both must be on the same MQTT broker address and port

Once connected, the device publishes to `hearth/devices/#` and Home Assistant discovers it automatically. This typically takes a few seconds.

**Still not working?** Check Hearth's Logs page for MQTT connection errors, or use the Local API option as a fallback.

confirm.title: Hearth Device Discovered
confirm.description:
A Hearth companion device **{name}** has been discovered via MQTT.

This will create:
- **Notification service** — send desktop notifications from automations
- **Media player** — control media playback on your PC
- **Sensors & commands** — are published via MQTT auto-discovery and will appear automatically

Would you like to add this device?

local_api.title: Connect via Local API
local_api.description:
Enter the IP address of the PC running Hearth. This must be the PC's network IP (not 127.0.0.1, since this runs inside Home Assistant).

**Note:** The Local API only supports notifications. For full functionality (media player, sensors, commands), use MQTT auto-discovery instead.

The Local API must be enabled in Hearth: **Settings → Companion → Local API → Enable**. Default port is 5115.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the Hearth device at that address. Make sure Hearth is running, the Local API is enabled (Settings → Companion → Local API), and the IP address is reachable from Home Assistant.

abort.no_serial_number: The device did not provide a serial number — it may be running an older version of Hearth.
